text:
Sean Walker was never drafted, bounced through Los Angeles, Philadelphia and Colorado, and won the Stanley Cup with Carolina last spring. At 32 he's playing 21 minutes a night and producing like a top-pair defenseman: 11 points in 21 games, three goals in his last ten.

Some caution belongs here. His scoring rate, 1.5 points per 60, is well above the 1.15 our talent range expects, and the Hurricanes have scored 5.6 more goals than their chances deserved with him on the ice. Carolina owns the puck with him out there (60% of shot attempts at five-on-five), but that's partly the team: it does even better without him, and Evolving-Hockey noted last season that his teammates rank in the 96th percentile by impact, which flatters raw numbers.

What's his own is the defending. Evolving-Hockey had him taking away chances at an 86th-percentile rate once teammates are accounted for, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him stopping 15% of the entries aimed at him, against 11% for a typical defenseman. He's blocked 42 shots already. The points will probably settle; the defense is why he plays 21 minutes.
headline: Walker, the undrafted champion, is scoring
